safi-cedvel:1-4.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) redundant (zāʾida) [Note: It was said that (لا) is not redundant but is for negation, and there are two explanations of that: the first, that it negates swearing by the Day of Resurrection and by the self-reproaching soul; the second, that it is a rejection of implied speech, as though they had said "You are fabricating against Allah concerning the resurrection", so He said "No", then began with the oath.. And it has parallels in the speech of the Arabs.]; (بيوم) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أقسم), and likewise (لا أقسم بالنفس ...).
The clause «أقسم ...» has no grammatical position: an opening clause (ibtidāʾiyya).
The clause «أقسم (the second)» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the opening clause.. And the answer of the oath for both clauses is omitted, indicated by what follows it, i.e. لتبعثنّ "you will surely be raised".
3- (الهمزة) for interrogation of reproach and rebuke; (أن) lightened from the heavy form (mukhaffafa min al-thaqīla), its noun being the pronoun of the matter (ḍamīr al-shaʾn), omitted [Note: Its noun may be the first-person plural pronoun of majesty, i.e. أنّنا لن نجمع ...].
The clause «يحسب الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «لن نجمع ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar (predicate) of the lightened (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن لن نجمع ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسب.
4- (بلى) an answering particle affirming a negated question, i.e. "yes, We shall gather them"; (قادرين) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the fāʿil (agent) of the implied verb; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative ...
The interpreted maṣdar (أن نسوّي ...) is in the position of a genitive by (على), attached to (قادرين).
The clause «(نجمعها) قادرين» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «نسوّي ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(اللوّامة): feminine of اللوّام, an intensive form (ṣīghat mubālagha) from the triliteral لام; its pattern is فعّال, and the feminine is فعّالة, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

* Rhetoric:
The art of sound division, or harmony between meanings: the saying of Allah the Exalted «لا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيامَةِ وَلا أُقْسِمُ بِالنَّفْسِ اللَّوَّامَةِ».
This verse is counted among the beauties of division, because of the harmony of the two things sworn by: He first swore by the Day of Resurrection, then swore by the souls that are requited in it, upon the reality of the resurrection and the requital.

safi-cedvel:5-6.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for transitional digression (al-iḍrāb al-intiqālī); (اللام) redundant (zāʾida); (يفجر) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن after the lām; (أمامه) an adverb borrowed for time — it was for place — accusative [Note: I.e. man wishes to continue in his wickedness in the time that lies ahead of him.]; (أيّان) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as an adverb of time, attached to (mutaʿalliq) a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (يوم).
The clause «يريد الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يفجر ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفجر ...) is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi (direct object) of the verb يريد — and this is the remote position —. The clause «يسأل ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of يفجر [Note: It may be an explanatory resumption.. or a badal (substitute) of the clause يريد.].
The clause «أيّان يوم ...» is in the position of an accusative as mafʿūl bihi of the verb يسأل, which is suspended (muʿallaq) by the interrogative, with a preposition implied.

* Morphology:
(5) أمامه: an adverbial noun of place — borrowed in the verse for time —; its pattern is فعال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.
(6) أيّان: an interrogative noun — and it may be conditional — used to indicate time; its pattern is فعّال, with fatḥa on the fāʾ.

safi-cedvel:7-10.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — attached to (mutaʿalliq) (يقول), and إذ is an adverbial noun in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi; (أين) interrogative noun, in the position of an accusative as an adverb of place, attached to a fronted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المفرّ).
The clause «برق البصر ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «خسف القمر ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause برق البصر.
The clause «جمع الشمس ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause برق البصر.
The clause «يقول الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
The clause «أين المفرّ ...» is in the position of an accusative: the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).

* Morphology:
(المفرّ): a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral فرّ [Note: It cannot be a noun of place, because that would have to be on مفعل — with kasra on the ʿayn — since its imperfect is يفرّ..]; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn; the vowel of the ʿayn was transferred to the letter before it to suit the doubling.

safi-cedvel:11-13.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) a particle of deterrence and rebuke against seeking flight; (لا) the lā of generic negation, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being موجود "existing"; (إلى ربّك) attached to an omitted fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (subject) (المستقرّ); (يومئذ) an adverb attached to (mutaʿalliq) the omitted khabar [Note: It may not be attached to المستقرّ: if it is a mīmī maṣdar, what it governs cannot precede it, and if it is a noun of place, it has no governing power.], and the second (يومئذ) is attached to (ينبّأ); (بما) attached to (ينبّأ)..
The clause «لا وزر ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «إلى ربّك.. المستقرّ.» has no grammatical position: giving the reason (taʿlīliyya).
The clause «ينبّأ الإنسان ...» has no grammatical position: an explanatory resumption (istiʾnāf bayānī).
The clause «قدّم ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the relative noun (ما).
The clause «أخّر ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the ṣila clause.

* Morphology:
(وزر): a noun meaning refuge or fortress; its pattern is فعل, with two fatḥas.

safi-cedvel:14-15.t:
* I'rab:
(بل) for digression (al-iḍrāb); (على نفسه) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (بصيرة) [Note: Or it is a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ بصيرة, with the omission of the thing described, i.e. "a seeing eye" or "seeing limbs", and the clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ الإنسان.], which is the khabar (predicate), and (التاء) is for intensiveness [Note: As one says "So-and-so is a حجّة (proof)" or "an عبرة (lesson)".. And الإنسان may be interpreted as the limbs.]; (الواو) circumstantial (ḥāliyya).
The clause «الإنسان.. بصيرة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «ألقى ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the pronoun in بصيرة..
And the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) is omitted, its implied form being: "they would not be accepted from him".

* Morphology:
(ألقى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is ألقي — with a yāʾ at its end —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(معاذير): plural of معذرة, irregularly [Note: See verse (165) of al-Aʿrāf.], and it is a collective noun on the view of al-Zamakhsharī..

safi-cedvel:16-19.t:
* I'rab:
(لا) prohibitive, making the verb jussive (majzūm); (به) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (تحرّك); (اللام) of reason (al-taʿlīl); (تعجل) imperfect verb, accusative by an implied أن.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن تعجل) is in the position of a genitive by the lām, attached to (تحرّك).
The second (به) is attached to (تعجل); (علينا) attached to the omitted khabar (predicate) of إنّ; (الفاء) conjunction, and the second is linking the apodosis.
The clause «لا تحرّك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تعجل ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the implied particle relative (أن).
The clause «إنّ علينا جمعه ...» has no grammatical position: giving the reason for the prohibition.
The clause «قرأناه ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «اتّبع ...» has no grammatical position: the apodosis of a non-jussive condition.
19- (ثمّ) a conjunction; (علينا) attached to the khabar of the second إنّ; (بيانه) noun of إنّ, accusative..
The clause «إنّ علينا بيانه» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause giving the reason.

* Morphology:
(قرآنه): maṣdar of the triliteral قرأ, annexed to its object, i.e. "your reciting it"; its pattern is فعلان, with ḍamma then sukūn.

* Benefits:
- The Prophet's ﷺ eagerness to memorize the Qur'an: This verse points to the Prophet's ﷺ intense eagerness to memorize the verses of revelation, so that they would not slip away from him.
It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbās, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ used to suffer hardship from the revelation, and he used to move his lips, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent down (لا تحرك به لسانك). So after that, when Jibrīl came to him, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would listen, and when Jibrīl departed, the Prophet ﷺ would recite it as he had recited it — and in one narration: as Allah the Exalted had promised him. This is the wording of al-Ḥumaydī. Al-Baghawī narrated it by way of al-Bukhārī, and said in it: When Jibrīl came down to the Prophet ﷺ with revelation, he was among those who moved his tongue and lips, and it was hard on him, and that was noticeable in him, so Allah the Mighty and Majestic sent down the verse: (لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ). He said: It is upon Us to gather it in your breast and that you recite it; (فَإِذا قَرَأْناهُ فَاتَّبِعْ قُرْآنَهُ): when We send it down, then listen; (ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا بَيانَهُ): it is upon Us to make it clear by your tongue. So when Jibrīl came to him he would lower his head, and when he left he would recite it as Allah the Exalted had promised him. And in one narration: he used to move his lips when it was revealed to him, fearing that it would slip away from him, so it was said to him: (لا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِ لِسانَكَ لِتَعْجَلَ بِهِ إِنَّ عَلَيْنا جَمْعَهُ وَقُرْآنَهُ), i.e. We gather it in your breast, and قرآنه, i.e. that you recite it.

safi-cedvel:20-21.t:
* I'rab:
(كلّا) for deterrence; (بل) for digression (al-iḍrāb); (الواو) for conjunction.
The clause «تحبّون ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «تذرون ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.

safi-cedvel:22-25.t:
* I'rab:
(وجوه) mubtadaʾ (subject), nominative [Note: Beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is qualified.], qualified by the naʿt (adjective) (ناضرة); (يومئذ) an adverb, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — annexed to the adverbial noun إذ.. attached to (mutaʿalliq) the naʿt ناضرة; (إلى ربّها) attached to the khabar (predicate) (ناظرة); (الواو) conjunction; (وجوه يومئذ باسرة) is like the first verse; (بها) attached to the passive verb (يفعل); (فاقرة) nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent).
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يفعل ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يظنّ.
The clause «وجوه ... إلى ربّها ناظرة» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «وجوه.. تظنّ ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تظنّ ...» is in the position of a nominative: khabar of the second mubtadaʾ (وجوه).
The clause «يفعل بها فاقرة» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(22) ناضرة: feminine of ناضر, active participle of the triliteral (نضر), on the pattern فاعل, and it is فاعلة.
(24) باسرة: feminine of باسر, active participle of (بسر), meaning "he frowned"; its pattern is فاعل.
(25) فاقرة: a noun for a calamity.. In al-Miṣbāḥ: "the calamity فقرت the man", i.e. befell him; its pattern is فاعلة.

* Benefits:
- Will the believers see their Lord in the Hereafter?
The scholars of Ahl al-Sunna said: The vision of Allah, Glorified and Exalted, is possible, not rationally impossible, and they agreed unanimously that it will occur in the Hereafter, and that the believers, not the disbelievers, will see Allah, Glorified and Exalted, as evidenced by the saying of the Exalted: (كَلَّا إِنَّهُمْ عَنْ رَبِّهِمْ يَوْمَئِذٍ لَمَحْجُوبُونَ). Groups among the Muʿtazila, the Khawārij and the Murjiʾa claimed that none of His creation will see Allah the Exalted, and that seeing Him is rationally impossible; but this claim of theirs does not rest on any evidence from the Book or the Sunna, but is based only on opinion and conjecture. The proofs of the Book and the Sunna, and the consensus of the Companions and of the early generations of the community after them, have combined to affirm the vision of Allah the Exalted. About twenty Companions narrated it from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and the verses of the Qur'an about it are well known, and the objection of the Muʿtazila has well-known answers in the books of the theologians of Ahl al-Sunna, and this is not the place to mention them. Further, the position of the people of truth is that vision is a faculty that Allah places in His creatures, and it does not require the meeting of rays, nor facing the thing seen, nor anything else.
As for the hadiths:
It is narrated from Ibn ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The lowest of the people of Paradise in rank is one who looks at his gardens, his spouses, his bliss and his servants over the distance of a thousand years' journey, and the most honoured of them with Allah is one who looks at His Face morning and evening." Then the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited: (وجوه يومئذ ناضرة إلى ربها ناظرة).
And from Jarīr ibn ʿAbd Allāh, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and he looked at the moon on the night of the full moon, and said: "You will see your Lord with your own eyes as you see this moon; you will not be crowded in seeing Him. So if you are able not to be overcome in missing a prayer before the rising of the sun and before its setting, then do so." Then he recited: (وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ قَبْلَ طُلُوعِ الشَّمْسِ وَقَبْلَ الْغُرُوبِ).
Moreover, other sound hadiths have come on this subject, which there is no room to present in full.

safi-cedvel:26-30.t:
* I'rab:
(إذا) attached to (mutaʿalliq) the apodosis indicated by His saying (إلى ربّك يومئذ المساق), and the fāʿil (agent) of (بلغت) is omitted, indicated by the context, namely the spirit or the soul; (الواو) conjunction in the three places; (من) interrogative noun, in the position of a nominative as mubtadaʾ (subject), its khabar (predicate) being (راق), which is nominative, the sign of the nominative being the implied ḍamma on the omitted yāʾ, for it is a defective noun (ism manqūṣ); (بالساق) attached to (التفّت); (إلى ربّك) attached to a fronted khabar of the mubtadaʾ (المساق); (يومئذ) an adverb of time, accusative — or indeclinable (mabnī) — attached to what the adverb إذا is attached to, so it is a badal (substitute) of it..
The interpreted maṣdar (أنّه الفراق ...) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of ظنّ.
The clause «بلغت ...» is in the position of a genitive, muḍāf ilayhi.
The clause «قيل ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause بلغت.
The clause «من راق ...» is in the position of a nominative: the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) [Note: It is originally the object of speech (maqūl al-qawl).].
The clause «ظنّ ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause بلغت..
The clause «التفّت الساق ...» is in the position of a genitive: conjoined to the clause بلغت..
The clause «إلى ربّك ... المساق» has no grammatical position: an explanation of the implied apodosis of إذا, i.e.:
"when it reaches the collarbones.. it is driven to the judgment of its Lord".

* Morphology:
(التراقي): plural of ترقوة, a noun for the upper bone that extends from the breastbone to the shoulder, or it is the front of the throat at the top of the chest where the breath rises; its pattern is تفعلة, with fatḥa on the tāʾ, the ʿayn and the lām, and the pattern of التراقي is تفاعل. In it there is a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is التراقو: what preceded the wāw had kasra, so it was turned into a yāʾ.
(راق): active participle of (رقي) or of (رقى): the first meaning "he ascended", of the pattern-class فرح, and the second meaning "he recited over him to cure him", of the pattern-class ضرب; its pattern is فاع. In it there is a weak-letter change by deletion (iʿlāl bi-l-ḥadhf) because of the meeting of two quiescent letters, so it is defective (manqūṣ).
(المساق): a mīmī maṣdar from the triliteral ساق; its pattern is مفعل, with fatḥa on the mīm and the ʿayn. In it there is a weak-letter change by conversion; its original form is مسوق, with fatḥa on the mīm and the wāw and a quiescent letter between them..
The fatḥa of the wāw was transferred to the sīn and the wāw was made quiescent — a weak-letter change by quiescence —; the sīn was vowelled with fatḥa before the wāw, so the wāw was turned into an alif — a weak-letter change by conversion —.

* Rhetoric:
The representational metaphor (al-istiʿāra al-tamthīliyya): in the saying of Allah the Exalted «وَالْتَفَّتِ السَّاقُ بِالسَّاقِ».
In the noble verse there is a representational metaphor for the severity of parting from what one is accustomed to — homeland, family, children and friend — and the severity of coming before one's Lord, majestic is His affair. The two severities have become entwined with each other, as the shank is entwined with the shank. And one says "the war bared its shank" as a metaphor for its severity.

safi-cedvel:31-33.t:
* I'rab:
(الفاء) resumptive; (لا) negative in both places; (لكن) a particle of rectification (istidrāk), inoperative (muhmal); (إلى أهله) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (ذهب).
The clause «لا صدّق ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «لا صلّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «كذّب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «تولّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كذّب.
The clause «ذهب ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كذّب or تولّى.
The clause «يتمطّى ...» is in the position of an accusative: ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of ذهب.

* Morphology:
(صلّى): the alif is converted from a yāʾ, and its origin is a wāw, because the plural of الصلاة is صلوات.. the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif; its pattern is فعّل.
(يتمطّى): the alif is converted from a yāʾ, and its origin is a wāw, for it is taken from المطا, which is the back; the wāw was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif; its pattern is يتفعّل.

safi-cedvel:34-35.t:
* I'rab:
(أولى) khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), its implied form being العقاب "the punishment" or الهلاك "destruction" [Note: Al-Maḥallī reported that (أولى) is a verbal noun with the sense of a past verb (ism fiʿl māḍin), meaning "evil after evil has come close to you", and the fāʿil (agent) is a latent (mustatir) pronoun referring to what is understood from the context, i.e. evil or what you dislike; the lām in (لك) is for clarification (al-tabyīn), so it is redundant, and the second-person pronoun is the mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and the second أولى is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, i.e. the content of the meaning of the first أولى.]; (لك) attached to (mutaʿalliq) (أولى); (الفاء) conjunction; the second (أولى) is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, its implied form being هو, i.e. the threat or the evil; (ثمّ) a conjunction..
The clause «(العقاب) أولى ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «(هو) أولى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause.
The clause «أولى لك ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the resumptive clause, for emphasis.
The clause «(هو) أولى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause أولى لك.

safi-cedvel:36-36.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation of reproach; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative; (سدى) ḥāl (circumstantial), accusative, of the pronoun of يترك.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يترك) is in the position of an accusative, standing in place of the two objects of يحسب.
The clause «يحسب ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يترك ...» has no grammatical position: the ṣila (relative clause) of the particle relative (أن).

* Morphology:
(سدى): a derived adjective for singular and plural; one says إبل سدى, i.e. neglected camels.. And (الألف) is converted from a yāʾ.. Al-ʿUkbarī said: the alif is converted from a wāw.. In al-Miṣbāḥ it comes: سديت الأرض فهي سدية, of the pattern-class تعب, "its dew became abundant"; and سدا الرجل سدوا, of the pattern-class قال, "he stretched his hand towards the thing"; and سدا البعير سدوا, "the camel stretched its foreleg in walking".. and أسديته "I left it سدى", i.e. neglected.

safi-cedvel:37-40.t:
* I'rab:
(الهمزة) for interrogation; (يك) imperfect verb, jussive (majzūm), and the sign of the jussive is the sukūn appearing on the nūn that is omitted for lightening; (من منيّ) attached to (mutaʿalliq) a naʿt (adjective) of (نطفة); and the pronoun is the noun of (كان), referring to المنيّ; and the fāʿil (agent) of (خلق) is a pronoun referring to Allah, and likewise (سوّى) and (جعل); (منه) attached to (جعل), by making it carry the meaning of خلق; (الذكر) badal (substitute) of الزوجين, accusative.
The clause «لم يك ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.
The clause «يمنى ...» is in the position of a genitive: naʿt of منيّ.
The clause «كان ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause لم يك.
The clause «خلق ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كان.
The clause «سوّى ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كان.
The clause «جعل ...» has no grammatical position: conjoined to the clause كان.
40- (الهمزة) is like the first; (قادر) genitive in form, accusative in position, khabar (predicate) of ليس; (أن) a particle that forms a maṣdar and makes the verb accusative.
The interpreted maṣdar (أن يحيي..) is in the position of a genitive by (على), attached to (قادر).
The clause «ليس ...» has no grammatical position: resumptive.

* Morphology:
(منيّ): a noun for the male's fluid ejected into the womb; its pattern is فعيل.
(يمنى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion (iʿlāl bi-l-qalb); its original form is يمني: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(سوّى): it contains a weak-letter change by conversion; its original form is سوّي — with yāʾ at its end —: the yāʾ was vowelled after a fatḥa, so it was turned into an alif.
(الموتى): plural of ميّت.. see verse (28) of Sūrat al-Baqara.
